groups.sentence: Instructors state in the syllabus or remind students that they are responsible for the work they submit.
Students take responsibility for the accuracy, quality and content of the AI-assisted work they submit.
Students are responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive or unethical content from an AI query that they submit.
Students are responsible for any errors or omissions the AI tool produces in the work they submit.
Human authors are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of AI-assisted code and research outputs.
Faculty and staff are responsible for the accuracy of the content and work products they produce with AI.
Inaccurate or poor AI-assisted work will be graded accordingly, with reduced credit.
Everyone is responsible for the content they produce, publish or share with AI assistance.
Everyone is accountable for the decisions, actions and outcomes that result from their use of AI.
Responsibility stays with the human author and cannot be shifted to the AI tool or the university.
Everyone is the author and owner of AI-assisted work and owns it as their own.
Students are responsible for how they use AI, including using it ethically and appropriately.
Students understand they are ultimately responsible for their submissions and take ownership of them, even when AI is used.
